newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended sharply down on Tuesday on long liquidation with the approach of the January delivery date, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,025 yuan ($364) per tonne, down 65 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,000 and hit a high of 3,060.
March fell 81 to 2,995, May 29 to 3,091, July was unchanged at 3,170, September fell 94 to 3,264 and November 98 to 3,300.
Combined volume fell to 10,700 tonnes from 17,100.
Traders said many investors liquidated their long position because they did not want to take physical goods.
"Long liquidation was responsible for today's falls, with many investors not wanting to hold positions with the approach of the New Year and the delivery date of January contract," one trader said.
"Soybean is likely to fall further in the next few days due to long liquidation," he added.
